error.signature: AI tells a New Zealand tenant that paying the bond to the landlord is the end of the process, with no need to confirm it was lodged with Tenancy Services

verdict.summary: In New Zealand a landlord who receives a bond must lodge it with Tenancy Services within 23 working days - not lodging it is against the law - so tenants need to actively confirm lodgement rather than assume the landlord is simply holding the deposit.

dead_ends.action: Pay the bond straight to the landlord and assume that's the end of it, like a security deposit held by the landlord directly in many other countries
dead_ends.why_fails: Under NZ law the landlord must lodge the bond with Tenancy Services within 23 working days of receiving it; not doing so within that timeframe is against the law and can lead to a financial penalty for the landlord, and tenants who never check often only find out when a dispute arises and there's no lodged bond to draw on.
dead_ends.common_misconception: The landlord is allowed to just keep the bond themselves as long as they return it at the end.

dead_ends.action: Assume that once you've paid the bond, there's nothing left to verify
dead_ends.why_fails: Lodgement is the landlord's legal obligation, not something a tenant is automatically shown proof of - Tenancy Services advises tenants to contact the landlord if they don't receive lodgement confirmation.
dead_ends.condition: Applies whenever a bond is paid directly to a landlord rather than lodged online jointly

workarounds.action: Ask the landlord to confirm the bond has been lodged with Tenancy Services, and follow up if you don't hear anything within a few weeks
workarounds.how: Tenancy Services normally sends confirmation once a bond is lodged; if nothing arrives within about 6 weeks, contact the landlord directly and, if still unresolved, contact Tenancy Services.

workarounds.action: Know the legal caps so you can spot an unlawful bond amount up front
workarounds.how: A landlord can charge at most 4 weeks' rent as bond, plus up to 2 weeks' rent as a separate pet bond if you have a pet.
